  Readable gloss: "Naioth (נָיוֹת) designates a location in or near Ramah, associated with Samuel and a community of prophets. When David fled from Saul, he came to Samuel 'at Naioth in Ramah' (1 Sam 19:18). Saul sent three groups of messengers to seize David, but each time the Spirit fell upon them and they prophesied (1 Sam 19:19-21). Saul himself went and likewise prophesied all day and night (1 Sam 19:22-24). David then fled from Naioth to Jonathan (1 Sam 20:1). The name likely derives from naveh ('dwelling'), suggesting a communal prophetic residence."

    Enriched: A place name for the prophetic community's abode in or near Ramah, where Samuel presided. Appears exclusively in David's flight from Saul (1 Sam 19:18-23; 20:1). Notable for the repeated outpouring of the Spirit that caused Saul's messengers and Saul himself to prophesy involuntarily. The name likely derives from naveh ('dwelling').
    Existing Spanish translations: Nayot, a-Nayot, de-Nayot, en-Nayot
